title: Introduce rate-controlled eval fanout and stability throttle
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: intermittent test flakiness and noisy regression alerts were traced to large parallel fanouts in nightly eval runs that overwhelm downstream evaluators and expose non-deterministic scheduler behavior. This PR introduces a rate-controlled eval fanout implementation plus a stability throttle CI hook that applies per-cohort backpressure and soft-quarantine for noisy probes to reduce false-positive regression gates.

What this changes: adds a new fanout layer that emits evaluation tasks at a configurable token/req/sec rate, implements cohort-level token-bucket throttles and exponential backoff for transient failures, and wires a CI hook that can mark a failing cohort as 'degraded' instead of failing the entire gate. Configuration is exposed via eval-config.yaml with sensible defaults so existing pipelines are backwards compatible.

Key features: rate limiter with burst allowance, per-cohort sliding success window, dynamic soft-quarantine (n-fails -> mirror-only for M minutes), stability score emitted to telemetry, and a CI adapter which downgrades failures to warnings when degradation thresholds are met. Includes documentation and an examples/ci-config snippet for teams to opt-in.

Testing and validation: unit tests for throttler and fanout runner; an integration test that simulates 10x traffic spike and verifies downstream worker concurrency stays within configured bounds; load bench shows median CI gate latency unchanged and 78% reduction in transient regression noise on a 2-week historical replay.

Rollout plan: merge behind feature flag (eval.rate_fanout.enabled=false) and enable for canaries in the nightly-eval pipeline. Monitor metrics (eval/fanout/request_rate, eval/cohort/stability_score) for 48h before wider enablement.

Checklist:
- [x] Tests added (unit/integration)
- [x] Docs updated (docs/eval/ops.md)
- [x] Telemetry events instrumented
- [x] Feature gated for staged rollout

Related: ENG-91234 (reduce noisy CI regressions), ENG-94021 (eval pipeline hardening).

review_comments: Arjun Patel (2025-01-18): Overall this looks solid. A couple of safety asks: ensure the default rate limits are conservative for hosted CI (we don't want to throttle customer-facing jobs). Please add a metric on 'throttled_requests' and a short circuit so a downstream worker that's healthy can opt-out of throttling.
Maya Chen (2025-01-18): Added throttled_requests counter and opt-out flag (fanout.runner.allow_direct_when_healthy). Updated tests to cover the case where downstream reports healthy=true.

Elena Torres (2025-01-19): Found a race in the token_bucket when refilling under concurrent access. Suggest switching to monotonic time and adding a small jitter on refill to avoid thundering herd. Also requested a doc blurb on how soft-quarantine interacts with rollback policies.
Maya Chen (2025-01-19): Fixed refill race by moving to time.monotonic and added jitter; expanded docs section. Re-ran integration test locally (attached bench logs).

Samir Khan (2025-01-20): CI integration initially failed on lint due to formatting; after a prettier run and a small test fix CI is green. Approving pending renaming one config key to be more explicit.
Maya Chen (2025-01-20): Renamed eval.rate_fanout.max_burst -> eval.rate_fanout.burst_capacity and pushed a tiny follow-up commit.
release_notes: Adds an opt-in rate-controlled evaluation fanout and a stability throttle CI hook to reduce transient regression noise; feature is behind feature flag eval.rate_fanout.enabled. See docs/eval/ops.md for configuration and rollout guidance.
